paper.title_en: APOLLO-Timing: Annealed Phase - Orbit Lattice Linking across Observations for Binary Pulsar Timing
paper.abstract_en: Sparse observations of binary pulsars can leave the orbit and the pulse count across observing gaps uncertain. We present APOLLO-Timing, a Bayesian phase-orbit lattice method that fits timing parameters together with integer pulse offsets between observing sessions. To validate candidate phase connections, we refit the timing model at fixed pulse numbers using the Python pulsar timing package PINT. We demonstrate the method on PSR J1912-1215, discovered in the CRAFTS survey. A preliminary Keplerian fit to variations in the apparent spin period and its derivative did not phase-connect 96 times of arrival (TOAs) spanning 1438.07 days in 23 sessions. Starting from its position, spin frequency $F_0$, and first time derivative $F_1$ estimated in that fit, with dispersion measure fixed, APOLLO-Timing recovers the orbit and a unique best-supported phase-connected solution without supplied orbital parameters. A repeat full-data blind search recovers the same pulse counts in 914.0 s, including the final fit. Setting the initial $F_1$ to zero in the 17-, 18-, and 19-session subsets also recovers the reference path. The solution gives $P_b=17.526$ days, $x=23.448$ light-seconds, $e=2.65\times10^{-5}$, $χ^2=188.01$, and a weighted rms residual of $5.08\,μ\mathrm{s}$. For a pulsar mass of $1.4\,M_\odot$ and inclination of $60^\circ$, the inferred companion mass is $0.67\,M_\odot$, favoring a CO/ONeMg white dwarf.
